messages:
anika: Heads-up — nightly perf alerted on Llama-2-70b (A100): p99 latency jumped ~18% when torch.compile + CUDA graphs are enabled. Attaching short profile dump.

samir: repro steps?

anika: Run on dedicated perf node: docker rwd/runtime:nightly, env TORCH_COMPILE=1, CUDA_GRAPHS=1, batch-slicing enabled. nvprof/NSIGHT shows the MHA kernel selection changed during warmup: previously we pick fmha_fast_fwd, now we end up with fallback_kernel_small_seq after a capture.

mike: my hunch — torch.compile + graph capture specialize to the concrete shapes seen during initial micro-batches. If batch-slicing trims sequences to 96 for warmup, the captured cudagraph binds kernels optimized for 96, and later requests at seqlen=128 hit a slower path (or force software fallback).

anika: I also noticed KV cache hit-rate dips during the same window: kv_cache.reset_count=3 in logs during the first 2000 tokens. Might be related — cudagraph replay can change pointer lifetimes/copy patterns.

jordan: Can we validate by forcing cudagraph re-warmup on shape change? Quick test: export CUDA_GRAPHS_FORCE_WARMUP=1 and add runtime guard: if (captured_graph.seq_len != current_seq_len) invalidate_graph().

rachel: ran that combo (FORCE_WARMUP=1 + torch._dynamo.config.dynamic_shapes=True). p99 returned near baseline, throughput down ~3% though. Logs showed: `mha_kernel: selected=wv_fmha_opt, fallback=false` after rewarm.

ci-bot: Perf CI: nightly/llama70b — baseline p99 -> +18% regress, after rewarm flags p99 -> +2% regressed. See artifacts: /ci/artifacts/1801001234/profile.zip :mag:

samir: Plan: (1) add runtime guard to invalidate/recapture cudagraphs on seqlen or batch-size skew; (2) teach autotuner to include "capture-binding" as a dimension when scoring kernel candidates (so it prefers kernels that are robust when captured); (3) add a micro-test that simulates warmup mix (mixed seqlens) to catch this. I'll open a PR. :spiral_notepad:

anika: also include a KV-cache pointer-stability test (we saw a rare segfault before when a capture kept stale device ptrs).

mike: I'll review the PR and run perf dash checks. cc rachel for dashboard verification.

rachel: noted. I'll add a dashboard panel to show kernel-selection by seqlen over warmup window so we can spot sudden switches.

anika: Thanks — please tag this with release-blocker if we can't get p99 < +5% by next deploy.
